about: The frontier release plate (callo 0.3.0): accuracy against per-decision latency on test-s1 (376 questions), callo's thinking budgets beside trained decision heads. callo arms are calibrations with --cache on (the default): Tiel-Coder, Dirk, Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma-4-E4B measured on the first build (2026-10-10) and refit offline on the refit build (the temperature grid widened to 0.25..16; Tiel, Dirk and Qwen budget entries byte-identical, Gemma keeps T 3.909); Sharp-MiniCPM5-2B re-measured on the readout-fix build (its T fit equals the refit's); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Sharp) at budgets 0 and 256, measured on the early-exit build (with the convergence probe) and its profile rebuilt with the gate reads on the gate-reads build. Only thinking-budget points are plotted (Tiel-Coder's early-exit point comes from its own calibration, plate/release-tiel-ee, on the gate build): early exit is opt-in and never picked, so the profiles' early-exit points stay off the chart and one fine-print line states the measured z .95 + gate point. Clef arms: Clef-Flash on llama.cpp's native Clef path (BF16, the reference) and on its release runtime, Clef 27B (our quant), Kev-9B; the Q4 Clef-Flash control and ggml-org's Clef Q4_K_M are reported in FIGURES.md only. CyberDirk is not on this plate; it is reported on its own model card. Label sides are art-directed: Flash-Next's label at its line's start (above callo's pick), Tiel-Coder's and Dirk's at their lines' ends. Paths are relative to the results root, given to `frontier.py build` as --root; callo_commits are commits of callo's development history, which the plate names by role (data/builds.json).
title: Tiel-Coder ties Clef-Flash without thinking, *a short think passes it*
subtitle: The same 376 test items, one decision at a time. Callo reads the answer from the served model's own log-probabilities; its points are thinking budgets.
